attributes.name: [OpenRouter] Provider Latency Regression
attributes.description: Alerts when the p99 end-to-end latency for any provider exceeds a configurable threshold. Detects provider-side degradation before it impacts end-user experience.

esqlQuery.esql:
// Alert when any provider's p99 latency exceeds a threshold in milliseconds.
// Default: 5000ms (5 seconds). Adjust per your SLO.
FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-*
| WHERE openrouter.performance.p99_latency IS NOT NULL AND openrouter.performance.provider IS NOT NULL
| STATS max_p99_ms = MAX(openrouter.performance.p99_latency) BY openrouter.performance.provider
| WHERE max_p99_ms > 5000
| SORT max_p99_ms DESC

investigation_guide.blob:
## Provider Latency Regression

### Triage Steps
1. Open the OpenRouter Performance dashboard and inspect the p99 latency trend per provider.
2. Identify which provider is degraded:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | WHERE @timestamp > NOW() - 3 HOURS | STATS p99 = MAX(openrouter.performance.p99_latency) BY openrouter.performance.provider | SORT p99 DESC`
3. Check whether the affected provider also shows lower throughput:
   `FROM metrics-openrouter.performance-* | STATS tput = AVG(openrouter.performance.p50_throughput) BY openrouter.performance.provider`
4. Consider switching to a different provider via OpenRouter's fallback routing.

### Common Causes
- Provider-side capacity constraints or incidents
- Large model deployment rollout at the provider
- Network congestion between OpenRouter and the provider
- Cold-start latency for low-traffic models

### Tuning
- Raise the threshold (e.g., `10000` = 10s) if your workload uses large models with inherently high latency.
- Alert per-model instead of per-provider by replacing `BY openrouter.performance.provider` with `BY openrouter.performance.model`.
